findings.summary: Keeping the inviter anonymous until acceptance undermines 'explicit consent': the invitee must accept a connection without knowing who they are connecting to, so the consent is not informed and a forwarded code lets an unintended recipient connect blindly to the owner.
findings.evidence: "Invitation-based pairs formed by two explicit consents; the inviter stays anonymous until acceptance" / "an unaccepted invitation never reveals the inviter"

findings.summary: The new rule says a forwarded code 'exposes nobody', but it does not say how the code is bound to the intended recipient. Any holder of a forwarded code can still accept it and then learn the inviter's identity, so the claimed protection is incomplete.
findings.evidence: "Opening the invitation does not reveal who sent it until it has been accepted, so a forwarded code exposes nobody"
